author: linos
text:
Hi, some words for you from my head. In my opinion I dont think the
ITs are doing complicated things in order to take peoples money,
otherwise it would be very hard to interact with each other in their
gang-stop-loss-mugging. I think they dont strive to make their ways
complicated as such but rather strive to hide their ways. In the end ,
look for the simple yet hidden things to the masses ( whole point in
RTM)

And maybe as you trade , remember these encouraging words by IF:

"Some perfect trades make you big profits. Some perfect trades make you
small or no profits. Some perfect trades even make you small losses,
when some bugger's messed with your PA!"

I truly wish you all the best.

Dengaima,

within 1 month (let me repeat, ONE MONTH
 ), you, sir, have come up with the above expressions. I can
sympathise with and feel you very much, but i dont wanna do that.
instead, i really really really want to congratulate you!.... You really
 are going super duper FAST & FURIOUS.

Aran, for one, listened to my frustration (just like yours) maybe around
 half a year ago, but his message is simple: "Just keep going and don't
give up, you'll definitely get there", then i asked him how, but somehow
 non-answer actually led & helped me move pass my own mental
barriers. So let this same message also come to you.

If you dont mind, i'd like to share my experience: RTM materials are
basic. Whenever i was lost reading someone's journal and following their
 style of trading, i'd most often come back to the basic. I read lots of
 people's journal, esp. the master traders, incl. Salivan's. The result
was confusions and not knowing what to do. I was stuck for a few months
there, like a hamster running on wheel. Then i decided to take my mind
off for a while and come back to RTM basics, IF's journal, and
especially IF's youtube videos (+lite course videos, afterwards) and
stopped looking at others journal. Somehow after a period of time, by
working out on my own charts just simply applying the basics, i found
kind of like "an eye" that allows me to see price with my own brain that
 I can't explain to anyone else. even if i really want to, i just can't.
 i tried sharing it a few times to some people, but instead of helping i
 was doing the opposite and felt really bad. I thought maybe i'm not
good at explaining things. Anyway, It's not perfect yet, but by
rehearsing/exercising "our eye", we can get better by ourselves.

What follows afterwards, reading others journal (incl. Salivan's),
things start to make sense, not from their perspective though, but
rather from my own perspective. So maybe, just maybe, we need to pave
our own path first before walking the path of others.

Again, I could be wrong and am open to other variables that may cause
setbacks in the above. So, the seniors are very much welcome to help us.

You'll never be alone, bro. I know some (incl.me) who have expressed the same words.

author: dengaima
text:
Strautum

I have also come to same conclusion. No matter what others do you cannot
 be them, even if you learn to copy the way they trade. It will never be
 yours truly as you never understood his/her thoughts at the time of of
trade and before trade analysis. Even though Salivan tried his best to
explain the way he trades.

At times it made sense other times it was just like wtf :)

Let's take an example for cooking. You learn how to use knife which cuts
 to make, temperature control and other techniques. However to reach
Michelin star rating you will need to experience the process of testing
and creating new recipes.

Therefore I would like to conclude that in order to be able reach
mastery level of pricr reading, learn the basics (markepedia,
fxsniffer's blogspot, ifmyante's videos) you can go through master's
journals but beware it might confuse you more, like it did to me.
However, I am sure you will get something out of each of master's
journals even if its 1 point that EUREKA moment for you. Maybe that 1
point is what you need to advance.

After all those information are in your brain, let them seep thoroughly
in your brain, live charts basically...always try to imagine the market
scenarios in your mind and imagine how it would play out based on Its
thinking. For example BSZ and Salivan's trendline break FO/NO examples.

Another thing, if you get new ideas based on teachings of RTM don't be afraid to investigate it and see if it makes sense.

It is long and arduous journey, but lucky we have RTM

Dengaima

author: Atari
text:
Hi Andrew, just visiting your journal and taking a peep. First of
all, take your time and work at your own pace. Understanding the market
 comes with time. I joined RTM in Sept. 2016 (but have been in the
market for almost 5 years now) and believe me, I have put in thousand of
 hours trying to learn and figure out the market. I went through all
the videos, non-masters and master's journals, and took notes and
review them. After awhile, I was still lost and could not see the
market. One one point, I thought I got it, but then realized that I did
not get it and was more confused than ever. After sometimes, things
begin to click naturally and "aha moments" start to appear. I started
to see the market clearer. This comes with time, constantly learning,
reviewing it over and over again until it clicks, and taking time off to
 let your brain absorb the material. What made my learning process
quicker is through teaching others. When I teach others, I really have
to understand the material otherwise, I will teach people the wrong
thing. Therefore, I had to be certain and confident that my answers
were right before teaching. The one thing that helped me is to"keep it
simple". Don't over complicate and over analyze, keep it simple. Learn
 the fundamentals in Markepedia and try to answer other people's
journals. Make an honest effort to answer your own questions first
using charts and draw out diagrams and post it here in your journal and
IF's journals (for the ones that you really tried to understand but
still struggling with). There will be senior members that will answer
them, only after they know you really tried hard to understand the
material in the first place. There is a saying that "To Master a Skill,
 you need at least 10,000 hours". The market is no different.
